topic.title: Steam games on my handheld
topic.question: What could get my Steam games onto my handheld?
topic.context: The handheld plays a few ported games well, but most of the Steam library still only runs on the PC. Nothing is decided yet: this is about finding ideas, not choosing one.

aims.line: Round 2. The hats have a few more first, then the council takes your ideas one at a time, and you put them in order.
goals: Play my whole Steam library away from my desk.
No fiddling: pick a game and play.
avoid: Hours of setup for games that run badly.

extras.line: From what you wrote, the hats had a few more. Kill any that miss.

ideas.text: A cosy mode: dim screen, quiet fans, one game you can play half asleep.
ideas.why: From your "Playing in bed without my PC on".

council.say: Soft and warm, like a book before sleep. This one feels like yours.
A dim screen hides small text in some games. Which games would it suit?

ideas.text: Stream at home, and port only the games you take outside.

council.say: This keeps both paths and puts each where it works. Close to the core.
Let the handheld learn which games you take outside, and port those first.

ideas.text: Your PC wakes itself when you open a game on the handheld.

council.say: Wake-on-LAN needs the PC plugged in and set up for it. What would happen when it's off at the wall?

ideas.text: Stream games from my PC when it's on.
ideas.from: From Yellow's spark: Does the game have to run on the handheld at all?

council.say: This goes straight at your first aim: your whole library away from the desk, with nothing ported.
Streaming needs your PC on and a strong connection, so away from home it struggles. What would make it work on the go?
Instant, nothing to set up, every game you own. That's the fun version.
Fast games lag, and the battery drains on wifi. Which games would you never stream?
Stream while the port downloads, then switch to the port when it's ready.

ideas.text: Get one game I own running, start to finish.

council.say: One full game proves the whole path, and the next one gets easier.
The first port takes the longest, and that's where people stop. What would keep you going?

ideas.text: A check that rates a game before I try to port it.
ideas.from: From Black's spark: Many games won't run on hardware this weak. What decides which ones will?

council.say: A rating needs reports of how each game runs on this hardware, and those exist mostly for popular games. Where would ratings for the rest come from?
Turn the rating into a shelf: ready tonight, worth a try, forget it.

ideas.text: Games with Steam Cloud already carry their saves between devices, so the handheld can pick up mid-game.

council.say: Picking up mid-level is the moment that makes it feel like your library.

ideas.text: My GOG games in the same list.
ideas.from: From Red's spark: What about your GOG games?

council.say: It widens the point from Steam to every game you own, still on your aim of playing away from the desk.
One list for every game you own is the dream version.

ideas.text: Don't port at all: stream from the PC and spend the effort on the controls.

council.say: It all rests on the PC being on and the connection holding. What's the plan for a train ride?

order.line: These made it through. Put them in your order; the decision round starts from the top.
